Site rollup lists the weakest pages first, which is what makes improvement continuous. Tested.

notes: CSRF via Laravel middleware (public endpoints exempted deliberately + protected by honeypot/throttle/signature); SQL injection prevented by Eloquent/PDO parameter binding throughout - no raw interpolation of user input; XSS mitigated by React escaping + the CSP below. SSRF: a REAL vulnerability was found and fixed in this stage - TechnicalSeoAuditor::crawl() fetched any tenant-supplied URL, so a tenant could read cloud metadata (169.254.169.254) or probe internal services using our server. UrlGuard now resolves the host and refuses loopback/private/link-local/reserved addresses, non-http(s) schemes and unusual ports, and redirects are not followed. Tested with the actual attack URLs.

A bug was found and fixed here - Organization soft-deletes, so delete() only stamped deleted_at, the cascadeOnDelete foreign keys never fired and the tenant's data survived an 'erasure'. Now forceDelete(); the test asserts with withTrashed() so a soft delete cannot pass as erasure. Deleting a user who SOLELY owns an organization is refused rather than stranding it. Requests are tracked as auditable data_requests rows.

Per-tenant retention_policies (audit logs, AI requests, outbound messages, intent signals, calls) applied by privacy:prune-expired-data with a --dry-run mode. Retention is OPT-IN: a subject with no active rule is kept indefinitely, so nothing is silently destroyed. Tested incl. the boundary (older pruned, recent kept) and the no-rule case.

feature: Consent tracking, communication opt-outs, email unsubscribe, SMS STOP handling
notes: Consent + opt-out is end-to-end from Stage 6: email_opt_in/sms_opt_in on contacts, one-click unsubscribe through our own /e/* endpoint writing to the suppression list, campaign sends filtered by suppression + opt-out (tested there). Policy acceptance tracking added here completes the consent record.

feature: Suppression lists, bounce and complaint handling, delivery tracking

feature: Support tickets: creation, status, priority, attachments, threaded communication
notes: Tickets with status/priority/category, assignment, threaded replies and resolution; INTERNAL NOTES are stored on the thread but stripped from every client-facing view (tested); replying to a resolved ticket reopens it (tested). QA 2026-08-20: ATTACHMENTS, named in this feature, are NOT implemented - tickets and ticket_messages have no attachment column, no ticket_attachments table exists, Ticket declares no files relation, and the only upload endpoint is the general library at /settings/files. The polymorphic files table could carry them but nothing wires a ticket to it, so §53's Attach File step cannot be performed. Downgraded from Tested to Partially Implemented because part of the stated scope is absent.

feature: Support impersonation: permissioned, visibly indicated, fully audited, time-limited
notes: Support impersonation - permissioned, visibly indicated, fully audited. Requires admin.impersonate + a mandatory reason; PLATFORM STAFF CAN NEVER BE IMPERSONATED (privilege-escalation guard); self-impersonation refused; the session is shared to the UI so a persistent banner always shows who is acting as whom; start and stop both audited with both user ids; stopping restores the operator and is deliberately ungated so nobody is trapped in a session. Every guard tested.

notes: PromptRegistry: prompts are versioned data, not literals. feature: AI cost tracking: requests, tokens, estimated cost per tenant/user/feature/provider/model
notes: Every call writes an ai_requests row (feature, provider, model, prompt/completion tokens, estimated cost in minor units from configured per-million pricing, duration, attempts, status, error, user). Cost attributable per tenant/user/feature via usageSummary(). Tested incl. cost arithmetic.

Limit::AiCredits (declared unenforced since Stage 3) is now ENFORCED by AiGateway through UsageMeter: the call is refused BEFORE reaching a provider when credits are exhausted, so overspend is impossible rather than merely visible. Professional 5,000 / Agency 20,000 / Enterprise unlimited. Tested: refusal incurs no provider call; one credit per successful call.

feature: AI error handling, retry behavior, auditability
notes: Bounded retry of transient provider failures only (timeout/429/5xx); permanent failures fail fast. Failures are recorded on the request row with the error and audited (ai.request.failed), are NOT billed as usage, and never silently substitute fabricated content. Tested: retry-then-succeed, fail-fast, no-billing-on-failure.

feature: Human confirmation for sensitive AI actions
notes: Human confirmation for sensitive AI actions. AI output that changes data or reaches a third party (update_crm/book_meeting/send_email) is only PROPOSED into ai_actions as pending; execute() refuses anything not confirmed by a user holding ai.actions.approve, rejection is terminal, execution is idempotent, and CRM writes are restricted to an allow-list of fields. No config flag permits autonomous execution. Tested extensively incl. permission enforcement and allow-list bypass attempt.

QA §21 step 6 ("Check Engagement") has nothing to hang on. WorkflowStep carries position, action_type, action_config and delay_minutes only, so a sequence is strictly linear and every enrolled contact runs every step. There is no condition, branch, split or exit criterion. Gap found by QA on 2026-08-19; it was not previously represented in the register. Pinned by tests/Feature/Qa/MarketingAutomationTest.php, which fails if workflow_steps gains a branching column, forcing this row to be revisited.

QA §21 step 2 ("Add Tag") has no implementation: no tags table, no contact_tag pivot, no tags column. Marked Not Applicable rather than Planned because marketing list membership already provides the same capability - static and dynamic lists label and segment contacts, and the workflow engine exposes it as add_to_list / remove_from_list (AUTO-026). Adding a parallel tag concept would duplicate it. Gap found by QA on 2026-08-19 and pinned by tests/Feature/Qa/MarketingAutomationTest.php.

feature: Ticket notifications to requester and assignee
notes: QA 2026-08-20: nothing in the delivery module notifies anyone. TicketService::open, reply and resolve write records and audit entries and send no notification, so a customer is never told their ticket was answered or resolved and must poll the portal, and staff are never told a ticket was raised. §53 names both 'Admin Receives Ticket' and 'Customer Receives Update'. NOTIF-006 covers business alerts (hot lead, new SQL, appointment, lead surge) and does not extend to support, so this was untracked. Pinned by tests/Feature/Qa/DeliveryPortalTest.php, which fails if a notification is ever dispatched.

feature: AI answers in the chat widget
notes: Free-text questions answered through AiGateway (credit cap, cost recording, audit) with a grounded chat.answer prompt; per-conversation turn cap; every failure degrades to the capture path. Mechanism tested on the fixture model per the Stage-12 honesty rule; answer quality requires a live provider key (ADR-0008).

ChatConversationSummarizer via AiGateway: 2-3 sentence takeover brief, auto-generated when a conversation goes live and on demand from the inbox. Internal notes are excluded from the transcript it sees. Cached until a new message; failures degrade to no-summary, never an error. Fixture-quality until a live AI key (ADR-0008).

Tenant-configured prompts (widget settings, up to 6) served only on the ai ask step and rendered as tappable chips; tapping sends the question as typed input. Old cached widgets ignore the field safely.
First question now offers Talk to a human; a free agent takes the chat live, otherwise the visitor is told what happens next and qualification continues so a person still gets full details.
